title: NOAA day-1 updates gave no clear storm probability score gain over day 3 on 804 matched days in 2023-2025
abstract: We joined NOAA planetary geomagnetic storm probabilities for the same target date in 2023-2025. On 804 dates with all three forecast leads, the day-3 to day-1 G1+ Brier score gain was 0.005329 (3.34%), with 95% 27-day block limits of -0.005853 to +0.016429. Mean probability minus event rate rose from 2.03 to 9.73 percentage points. G2+ and G3+ gains were also uncertain. Strict Kp>=5 changed the G1+ point estimate to a 9.34% loss. We account for this sign change exactly: 46 boundary days at Kp=4.667 had a mean probability increase of 0.153478, which raised the mean gain by 0.017562 under the rounded event rule. NOAA estimated Kp also gave an uncertain gain. These matched tests extend a prior calibration study on the same source data; they are not independent confirmation. Archive gaps, three years, few severe events and event-definition differences limit the result. We supply source hashes, a NOAA snapshot, code, aggregate results, a separate arithmetic audit and a figure. GFZ records remain external.

display.caption: Matched day-3 to day-1 changes on 804 days. Mean G1+ and G2+ error rises, but all score gain intervals include zero. GFZ rounded thresholds; pointwise 95% 27-day block intervals.

citations.reason: We reuse its frozen NOAA reports and GFZ vintage. Matched update scores and boundary attribution extend its lead-specific bias analysis on overlapping data.
